internet.q: Which part of a URL tells the browser which protocol to use?
internet.explain: The scheme (https://) tells the browser which protocol to use to talk to the server.

internet.q: A page generated fresh from a database on every request is called…
internet.explain: Dynamic sites build content at request time, often from a database.

opts: Maps domain names to IP addresses
internet.explain: DNS translates human-readable domain names into numeric IP addresses.

clientserver.q: Which HTTP status code means the resource wasn't found?
clientserver.explain: 404 Not Found means the server has no resource at the requested URL.
The client (browser) always sends the first request.

clientserver.q: Which HTTP method is typically used to submit form data that changes server state?
clientserver.explain: POST is conventionally used for submitting data that creates or changes something server-side.

html5.q: Which of these is an HTML5 semantic element?
html5.explain: <article> describes self-contained content, a semantic addition in HTML5.

html5.q: What does the HTML5 DOCTYPE declaration do?
opts: Puts the browser in standards mode for HTML5
html5.explain: <!DOCTYPE html> tells the browser to render using modern HTML5 rules.

html5.q: Which HTML5 feature removed the need for Flash in most video embeds?
html5.explain: The native <video> element plays media without third-party plugins.

structure.q: Which element holds content the visitor actually sees?

opts: In the browser tab and bookmarks
structure.explain: <title> sets the text shown in the browser tab and used for bookmarks/search results.

structure.q: Which attribute on <html> declares the page's language?
structure.explain: lang='en' (etc.) declares the document language for accessibility and SEO.

elements.q: Which attribute must be unique on the page?
elements.explain: id identifies exactly one element; class can repeat across many elements.

elements.q: Which of these is an empty (void) tag?
elements.explain: has no separate closing tag — it's a void element.

elements.q: Which of these is a block-level element by default?
elements.explain: <div> starts on a new line by default, unlike inline elements like <span> or <a>.

attributes.q: Which attribute adds a tooltip shown on hover?
attributes.explain: title text is displayed as a native tooltip on hover.

attributes.q: What prefix identifies a custom attribute intended for scripting?
attributes.explain: data-* attributes are the standard way to attach custom data to an element.

attributes.q: Which attribute disables a form control?
attributes.explain: disabled prevents interaction and excludes the field from form submission.

text.q: Which tag is used for the single most important heading on a page?
text.explain: <h1> is the top-level heading; there should usually be exactly one per page.

text.q: Which tag preserves whitespace and line breaks exactly as written?
text.explain: <pre> renders text in a fixed-width font and keeps spacing/line breaks intact.

text.q: Which tag semantically highlights text, like a highlighter pen?
text.explain: <mark> denotes text highlighted for reference or relevance.

lists.q: Which element pairs a term with its definition?
lists.explain: <dl> uses <dt> for the term and <dd> for its definition.

lists.q: How do you create a sub-list inside a list item?
lists.explain: Nesting a list element directly inside an <li> creates a sub-list.

lists.q: Which attribute changes what number an ordered list starts at?
lists.explain: start='5' makes the list begin counting at 5.

links.q: Which href value creates an email link?
links.explain: The mailto: scheme opens the visitor's default email client.

links.q: Which attribute combination safely opens an external link in a new tab?
links.explain: rel='noopener' prevents the new tab from accessing the opening page via window.opener.

links.q: What does an href value starting with # link to?
opts: A section on the same page
links.explain: A #fragment links to an element with a matching id on the current page.

images.q: What does the alt attribute do?
images.explain: alt text is shown if the image fails to load and read aloud by screen readers.

images.q: Which attribute lets the browser pick the best image for the screen size?
images.explain: srcset lists multiple image candidates so the browser can choose the best fit.

images.q: What is the purpose of loading='lazy' on an ?
opts: Defer loading offscreen images until needed
images.explain: Lazy loading defers fetching images until they're near the viewport, improving performance.

svg.q: Why use SVG instead of a JPEG/PNG for simple shapes?
opts: SVG stays crisp at any size
svg.explain: SVG describes shapes mathematically, so it scales without pixelating.

svg.q: Which element draws a straight line in SVG?
svg.explain: <line x1 y1 x2 y2> draws a straight line between two points.

svg.q: What does the viewBox attribute control?
opts: The coordinate system shapes are drawn in
svg.explain: viewBox defines the internal coordinate space, independent of the element's display size.

audio.q: Which attribute shows native play/pause controls?
audio.explain: controls displays the browser's built-in audio UI.

audio.q: Why is muted often required alongside autoplay?
opts: Browsers block autoplaying sound without it
audio.explain: Most browsers block autoplay with sound unless the media is muted.

audio.q: What does the loop attribute do on <audio>?
audio.explain: loop restarts playback automatically when the track ends.

video.q: Which attribute shows a preview image before a video plays?
video.explain: poster sets the image shown before playback starts.

video.q: Which element adds captions to a video?
video.explain: <track kind='captions'> links a caption file (e.g. WebVTT) to the video.

video.q: Why include width and height on a <video>?
opts: To reserve layout space and prevent content shifting
video.explain: Explicit dimensions reserve space before the video loads, avoiding layout shift.

opts: Embeds another page/document inside the current one
iframes.explain: <iframe> nests another HTML document inside the current page.

iframes.q: Why does an iframe need a title attribute?
iframes.explain: title gives assistive technology a readable label for the embedded content.

iframes.q: What does the sandbox attribute do on an iframe?
opts: Restricts what the embedded page is allowed to do
iframes.explain: sandbox applies a set of restrictions (like disabling scripts) to embedded, less-trusted content.

seo.q: What does the meta description tag control?
opts: The snippet shown under the title in search results
seo.explain: meta description supplies the summary text search engines often display.

seo.q: Why does alt text help SEO?
opts: It gives search engines readable text describing the image
seo.explain: Search engines can't 'see' images — alt text gives them (and screen readers) something to read.

seo.q: What does a canonical link tag prevent?
seo.explain: rel='canonical' tells search engines which URL is the authoritative version.

bestpractices.q: How many <h1> elements should a typical page have?
bestpractices.explain: A single <h1> gives the page one clear main heading for users and assistive tech.

bestpractices.q: Which is a best practice for long-term maintainability?
opts: Skipping alt text to save space
bestpractices.explain: Semantic structure and readable indentation make markup easier to debug and extend.

bestpractices.q: What does running markup through a validator help catch?
bestpractices.explain: Validators check markup against the HTML spec, flagging structural errors.

semantics.q: Which element should appear only once, holding a page's unique content?
semantics.explain: <main> wraps the unique content of a page and should normally appear exactly once.

semantics.q: What best describes when to use <article>?
opts: Content that could stand alone and be redistributed on its own
semantics.explain: <article> is for self-contained content — a blog post, comment, or news story — that would make sense on its own.

semantics.q: Which element creates a disclosure widget with no JavaScript?
semantics.explain: <details> with a <summary> child gives a native expand/collapse widget for free.

layout.q: What ARIA landmark role does <nav> map to automatically?
layout.explain: <nav> is exposed to assistive technology as the 'navigation' landmark automatically.

layout.q: What is the main purpose of a 'skip to main content' link?
opts: To let keyboard/screen-reader users bypass repeated navigation
To make the page load faster
layout.explain: It lets users jump straight past a repeated nav menu directly to the unique page content.

layout.q: In CSS Grid, what does `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr))` do?
opts: Lets the grid fit as many 200px+ columns as the space allows
layout.explain: auto-fit with minmax() lets the number of columns adjust automatically to the available width.

a11y-fundamentals.q: What alt text should a purely decorative image have?
a11y-fundamentals.explain: Empty alt (alt="") tells screen readers to skip the image entirely, which is correct for purely decorative images.

a11y-fundamentals.q: Why should positive tabindex values (like tabindex="3") generally be avoided?
opts: They override the natural tab order and can confuse keyboard users
a11y-fundamentals.explain: Positive tabindex values force a custom tab order that rarely matches visual/logical order, creating a confusing experience.

a11y-fundamentals.q: What is the first rule of using ARIA?
opts: Add ARIA to every element for safety
Don't use ARIA if a native HTML element already provides the needed semantics
ARIA replaces the need for alt text
a11y-fundamentals.explain: Native elements like <button> already have the right role and keyboard behavior built in — ARIA is for filling gaps, not replacing them.

forms.q: Inside a <form>, what does a plain <button> default to?
forms.explain: A <button> with no type attribute defaults to type="submit" inside a form — a common source of accidental submissions.

opts: Naming the group of controls inside a <fieldset>
A required attribute on every input
forms.explain: <legend> is the required first child of <fieldset> and announces what the group of controls represents.

forms.q: When must a form's enctype be set to multipart/form-data?
opts: When the form includes a file upload
forms.explain: File uploads require multipart/form-data so the browser can send binary file content correctly.

forminputs.q: Which input type gives a native slider control?
forminputs.explain: type="range" renders as a slider between a min and max value.

forminputs.q: What does the pattern attribute do?
opts: Sets a background pattern via CSS
Enforces a custom format using a regular expression
forminputs.explain: pattern takes a regular expression the input's value must match before the form can submit.

forminputs.q: Which input type is best for a phone number field?
forminputs.explain: type="tel" triggers the right mobile keyboard; phone formats still need a pattern since they vary internationally.

formvalidation.q: What does the novalidate attribute do when added to a <form>?
opts: Removes all inputs from the form
formvalidation.explain: novalidate turns off the browser's automatic constraint validation, letting a page implement fully custom validation instead.

formvalidation.q: Which CSS pseudo-class matches a field that currently satisfies all its constraints?
formvalidation.explain: :valid matches any form control whose current value passes its constraint validation.

opts: Clears a custom error, allowing the field to become valid again
Disables validation for that field only
formvalidation.explain: Passing an empty string to setCustomValidity() clears any custom error previously set on that field.

tables.q: What does the scope="col" attribute on a <th> do?
opts: Tells assistive technology the header describes the entire column below it
tables.explain: scope="col" (or "row") tells screen readers which cells a header cell applies to.

tables.q: Which attribute merges a table cell across multiple rows?
tables.explain: rowspan="n" makes a cell occupy n rows vertically; colspan does the equivalent across columns.

tables.q: Where must <caption> appear in a table?
tables.explain: <caption> must be the first element inside <table>, right after the opening tag.

a11y-standards.explain: WCAG is the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines, maintained by the W3C.

a11y-standards.q: Which WCAG conformance level is most commonly targeted in practice?
a11y-standards.explain: Level AA is the most common baseline referenced by organizational policies and legal requirements.

a11y-standards.q: Why is manual testing (keyboard, screen reader) still necessary alongside automated tools?
opts: Automated tools only catch a fraction of real accessibility issues
Manual testing is required by law everywhere
Automated tools don't work on HTML
a11y-standards.explain: Automated scanners are estimated to catch only around 30-40% of real accessibility issues — things like illogical focus order need a human to find.

responsive-structure.q: What happens on mobile browsers without a viewport meta tag?
opts: The page renders at a fixed desktop width and zooms out
responsive-structure.explain: Without it, mobile browsers assume a wide desktop layout and zoom the whole page out to fit, making text tiny.

responsive-structure.q: What does a mobile-first approach to media queries mean?
opts: Writing base styles for small screens first, then adding min-width queries for larger ones
Writing desktop styles first and overriding them for mobile
responsive-structure.explain: Mobile-first starts with small-screen base styles and layers on complexity as the viewport grows, via min-width media queries.

responsive-structure.q: Why does the flex `order` property need care regarding accessibility?
opts: It doesn't work in most browsers
It changes visual order only — screen readers and tab order still follow the HTML source order
It automatically fixes tab order too
responsive-structure.explain: order changes how content looks, not the underlying source order that keyboard/tab navigation and screen readers rely on.

css-intro.q: Which method of adding CSS is generally recommended for a multi-page site?
opts: An internal <style> block on each page
css-intro.explain: External stylesheets are cacheable and reusable across every page that links them, keeping markup clean.

css-intro.q: What is the correct syntax for a CSS comment?
css-intro.explain: CSS comments use /* ... */, unlike HTML's <!-- --> or JavaScript's //.

css-intro.q: When two rules have equal specificity, which one wins?
opts: The one that appears later in the stylesheet
css-intro.explain: On a specificity tie, the cascade falls back to source order — the later rule wins.

css-selectors.q: Which selector has the highest specificity?
css-selectors.explain: ID selectors outrank class selectors, which outrank type/element selectors; the universal selector has the lowest specificity of all.

css-selectors.q: What does `div > p` select, that `div p` would not?
opts:
Only

elements that are direct children of a

Only the first

in the document
css-selectors.explain: The child combinator (>) only matches direct children, while a plain space (descendant combinator) matches at any nesting depth.

opts: Overrides normal specificity rules for that declaration
css-selectors.explain: !important overrides the normal cascade, which is powerful but should be used sparingly since it makes later overrides harder.

css-colors-backgrounds.q: What's the key difference between opacity and an rgba() alpha value?
opts: opacity fades the whole element including children; rgba alpha only fades that one color value
css-colors-backgrounds.explain: opacity affects the entire element and everything inside it, while an alpha channel in rgba()/hsla() only makes that specific color translucent.

css-colors-backgrounds.q: Which CSS function creates a smooth color transition as a background image?
css-colors-backgrounds.explain: linear-gradient() (and radial-gradient()) generate a gradient image on the fly, used as a background-image value.

css-colors-backgrounds.q: In hsl(340, 60%, 45%), what does the third value control?
css-colors-backgrounds.explain: hsl() takes hue, saturation, and lightness in that order — lightness is the easiest to adjust for consistent shade variations.

css-units.q: Why is rem often preferred over em for font sizing?
opts: rem is always relative to the root font-size, avoiding compounding when nested
em doesn't work in modern browsers
rem is the only unit supported on mobile
css-units.explain: em compounds against each nested parent's font-size, which can grow unpredictably; rem always refers back to the root, staying consistent.

css-units.q: What does calc(100% - 40px) let you do that plain percentages can't?
opts: Mix different units in one calculation
css-units.explain: calc() lets you combine units like % and px in a single expression.
vh is 1% of the viewport's height, regardless of any parent element's size.

css-typography.q: Why should a font-family list end in a generic family like sans-serif?
opts: It guarantees a fallback if none of the earlier fonts are available
css-typography.explain: The generic family at the end guarantees the browser always has something to fall back to.

css-typography.q: What does a unitless line-height value like 1.5 do?
opts: Scales proportionally to the element's own font-size
Only works with rem font sizes
css-typography.explain: A unitless line-height multiplies against the element's own font-size, scaling safely if font-size changes later.

opts: Load a custom font file for use in font-family
Resize all text on the page
css-typography.explain: @font-face declares a custom font so it can be referenced by name in any font-family list.

css-text-styling.q: Which three properties together are needed for the classic text-truncation-with-ellipsis effect?
opts: white-space: nowrap, overflow: hidden, text-overflow: ellipsis
css-text-styling.explain: All three are required together — text-overflow: ellipsis alone does nothing without the other two.

css-text-styling.q: Does text-transform: uppercase change the actual text content in the HTML?
opts: No — only the visual display changes
css-text-styling.explain: text-transform is purely visual; the underlying text (and what a screen reader announces, in most cases) stays as written.

css-text-styling.q: What does overflow-wrap: break-word help with?
opts: Letting a single long word break mid-word instead of overflowing its box
css-text-styling.explain: It allows unbreakable long words (like a long URL) to wrap within a narrow container instead of spilling out.

css-box-model.q: In the default content-box model, does padding add to an element's set width?
opts: No, padding is always outside the width
Yes — width sets only the content area, padding and border are added on top
Only border adds to width, not padding
css-box-model.explain: With content-box (the default), the box's rendered size is width + padding + border combined.

opts: Makes width/height include padding and border, so the set size is the final rendered size
css-box-model.explain: border-box makes the box you set the box you get, since padding and border are now included within that width/height.

css-box-model.q: When two block elements stack vertically, what happens to their margins?
opts: The larger of the two collapses into a single gap
css-box-model.explain: Adjacent vertical margins collapse — the browser uses the larger value, not the sum of both.

css-positioning.q: What makes an element eligible to be the reference point for an absolutely positioned child?
opts: Any element can be a reference point
The ancestor must have a position value other than static
The ancestor must have a fixed width
Only <body> can be a reference point
css-positioning.explain: An absolutely positioned element positions relative to its nearest ancestor with position: relative, absolute, fixed, or sticky — not a static one.

css-positioning.q: What's the key difference between position: fixed and position: sticky?
opts: fixed always stays in the viewport; sticky only sticks within its containing block once scrolled to its offset
css-positioning.explain: sticky behaves like relative until it hits its scroll offset, then behaves like fixed — but only within its own container's bounds.

opts: Which overlapping positioned element renders in front
css-positioning.explain: z-index resolves stacking order among overlapping positioned elements — higher values render on top.

css-flexbox.q: What does display: flex do to an element's direct children?
opts: Turns them into flex items arranged along a main axis
css-flexbox.explain: Every direct child of a flex container automatically becomes a flex item.

css-flexbox.q: Which property distributes items with equal space between them, edges flush?
css-flexbox.explain: justify-content: space-between pushes the first and last items to the edges, distributing remaining space between the rest.

opts: Items to flow onto multiple lines instead of squeezing onto one
css-flexbox.explain: Without flex-wrap, all flex items are forced onto a single line/column by default, shrinking to fit.

css-grid.q: What does the fr unit represent in CSS Grid?
opts: A fraction of the container's remaining free space
css-grid.explain: fr divides the container's remaining space proportionally among tracks.

css-grid.q: What does grid-template-areas let you do?
opts: Sketch a layout with named regions that items claim with grid-area
css-grid.explain: grid-template-areas defines a readable, named layout map directly in the CSS.

opts: A grid that automatically adjusts its column count based on available space
css-grid.explain: auto-fit combined with minmax() lets the grid reflow its own column count as the container resizes — no media query needed.

css-pseudo-classes.q: Which pseudo-class matches an element while the pointer is over it?
css-pseudo-classes.explain: :hover matches for as long as the pointer is positioned over the element.

css-pseudo-classes.q: What does :nth-child(odd) commonly get used for?
css-pseudo-classes.explain: :nth-child(odd) matches every odd-positioned sibling — a common pattern for alternating row colors.

css-pseudo-classes.q: What does :not(.disabled) do in a selector like button:not(.disabled):hover?
opts: Excludes elements with the disabled class from matching
css-pseudo-classes.explain: :not() excludes anything matching its argument, letting a rule apply to everything except that case.

css-pseudo-elements.q: What symbol distinguishes a pseudo-element from a pseudo-class in modern CSS?
css-pseudo-elements.explain: Modern syntax uses :: for pseudo-elements (like ::before) and : for pseudo-classes (like :hover), though older code sometimes uses a single colon for both.

css-pseudo-elements.q: What CSS property is required for ::before or ::after to render anything at all?
css-pseudo-elements.explain: Without a content property — even content: "" — a ::before/::after pseudo-element won't render.

css-pseudo-elements.q: What does ::first-letter typically get used for?
css-pseudo-elements.explain: ::first-letter targets just the first character of a text block, commonly used for a large decorative drop-cap.

opts: Links whose href attribute starts with https
css-attribute-selectors.explain: The ^= operator matches values that start with the given string.

opts: Any class attribute containing "btn" anywhere in its value
css-attribute-selectors.explain: The *= operator matches a substring appearing anywhere within the attribute's value.

css-attribute-selectors.q: How do you make an attribute selector's value match case-insensitively?
opts: Add a space and the letter i before the closing bracket

css-form-styling.q: What does appearance: none do when styling a <select> or button?
opts: Removes the browser's native OS-drawn styling as a clean base
css-form-styling.explain: appearance: none strips native styling so custom background, border, and padding can fully take over.

css-form-styling.q: Which part of form controls is notoriously hard to restyle consistently across browsers?
opts: A native <select>'s dropdown arrow and checkbox/radio glyphs
css-form-styling.explain: Borders and colors are easy to restyle; the native arrow/glyph rendering varies significantly by browser and OS.

css-form-styling.q: What's a common way to give a user immediate feedback while filling out a form field?
opts: Only showing errors after final submit
Pairing :valid/:invalid/:focus with color changes as they type
css-form-styling.explain: Styling based on the field's live validation state gives low-friction, immediate feedback before the user even submits.

css-variables.q: How do you declare a CSS custom property?
css-variables.explain: Custom properties use a double-dash prefix, like --brand-color: #c4406b;.

css-variables.q: What does var(--name, fallback) do if --name isn't defined?
opts: Uses the provided fallback value instead
css-variables.explain: The second argument to var() is a fallback used only if the custom property isn't defined.

css-variables.q: What's a key advantage of CSS custom properties over Sass/Less variables?
opts: They're live in the browser and can change at runtime, unlike build-time preprocessor variables
They only work with px units
css-variables.explain: A preprocessor variable is baked in at build time; a CSS custom property can be changed live, e.g. via a media query or JavaScript.

css-responsive.q: What does a mobile-first approach to media queries use?
opts: min-width queries to add complexity as the screen grows
css-responsive.explain: Mobile-first starts with small-screen base styles, then layers on more complexity via min-width media queries.

css-responsive.q: What does object-fit: cover do for an ?
opts: Stretches the image, distorting its aspect ratio
Scales the image to fill its box, cropping as needed without distortion
css-responsive.explain: object-fit: cover fills the box while preserving the image's aspect ratio, cropping any overflow.

css-responsive.q: What do container queries respond to, unlike traditional media queries?
opts: The size of the component's own container, not the whole viewport
css-responsive.explain: Container queries let a component adapt based on the space it's actually given, regardless of the overall screen size.

opts: A named sequence of style states at percentage checkpoints
css-animations.explain: @keyframes defines the steps of an animation from 0% to 100% (or from/to).

css-animations.q: Why are transform and opacity generally preferred for animating over properties like width or top?
opts: They animate smoothly without forcing the browser to recalculate page layout
css-animations.explain: transform and opacity can be animated efficiently by the browser, while properties like width/top force expensive layout recalculation on every frame.

css-animations.q: What does prefers-reduced-motion let a stylesheet respond to?
opts: A user's OS-level request for reduced motion
css-animations.explain: Respecting prefers-reduced-motion (usually by disabling or simplifying animations) is an accessibility best practice.

opts: Nothing — it runs automatically like an animation
A state change, such as :hover or a class toggle
css-transitions.explain: Unlike a @keyframes animation, a transition needs some state change to move from its starting value to its ending value.

css-transitions.q: What is the correct order of values in the transition shorthand?
css-transitions.explain: The shorthand order is property, then duration, then timing-function, then delay.

css-transitions.q: Why might transition: all be less ideal than listing specific properties?
opts: It can accidentally transition properties you didn't intend to animate, and can be costlier to render
css-transitions.explain: Being explicit about which properties transition is more predictable and can be more efficient than transitioning everything that happens to change.
